newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gas oil trade seen vigorous, naphtha flat.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gas oil trade seen vigorous, naphtha flat.

text.p: Gas oil was actively talked in Tokyo amid generally lethargic oil products trading, with several major oil firms eager to get rid of surplus stocks, traders said on Tuesday.
Although Japan has tended to export gas oil mostly from refineries on the southern island of Okinawa, some oil firms have recently started to ship cargoes from plants located around Tokyo.
Export prices were quoted at about $1.00 per barrel below the mean of Singapore quotes on an FOB (free on board) basis.
Open-spec naphtha was assessed at $203.00/$204.00 per tonne for second-half October delivery, after changing hands at $203.35 in late trading on Monday.
In spread trading, first-half October/second-half October was traded at minus $2.00 on Monday.

Sluggish olefine and polyolefine prices in Asia have yet to spark production cuts by petrochemical manufacturers in Japan, although they have injected a bearish tone into the region's naphtha markets, traders said.
